blocking_findings.finding: Virtualization is not genuinely IntersectionObserver-driven. Observer callbacks update private visiblePages, but PageSlotState.visible is never updated and the hook never schedules visible-page renders. The test bypasses IO by calling the public setVisiblePages escape hatch and manually invoking ensureRendered for arbitrary pages, so it cannot prove a real 200-slot scroll window, non-eager scheduling, or the production canvas ceiling.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Connect observer state to the rendered slot/active-page contract and visible-page scheduling, remove the production test-control escape hatch, and add a controlled IntersectionObserver test that emits real entries for a mixed-geometry 200-page document, asserts nonzero starts only near the observed window, no eager getPage/render calls, and a measured live backing-canvas count <=10 throughout scrolling.

blocking_findings.finding: Metrics correlation and ordering do not meet the contract. renderStart records effective.renderScale (zoom × DPR/cap) instead of the required logical scale. Concurrent cancellation paths can both record renderCancel before either settles because cancellation has no single-owner guard. The ordering test only asserts replacement-start > cancel, not replacement-start > cancelled-settle, despite that being the strict required sequence.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Record currentScale as scale while retaining post-cap backing dimensions, serialize/claim cancellation so each task gets at most one cancel and one settle, and assert the exact non-vacuous sequence start → cancel → cancelled settle → replacement start with strictly increasing seq, no stale completed settle, nonzero starts, and monotonic generations.

blocking_findings.finding: PdfPageView does not implement the required PDF.js v5 TextLayer update lifecycle. Every zoom recreates the layer after cancelling the previous instance; update() is never called, and the test merely defines a fake update method without asserting it. The async lifecycle also lacks a post-render stale guard.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Implement and test the real v5 render/update/cancel lifecycle: update the retained layer for compatible zoom/rotation changes, cancel and replace only when necessary, and use generation/cancellation guards after every async boundary so superseded layers cannot write stale content.

blocking_findings.finding: Document teardown and documentDestroy metrics are not exact. Cleanup calls both loadingTask.destroy() and the resolved PDFDocumentProxy.destroy(), although loading-task destruction owns the loaded document transport, and it records documentDestroy unconditionally even for loads that never produced a document. Tests assert only event presence, so double destruction and phantom destruction metrics are not detected.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Define one idempotent teardown owner per load, avoid double-destroying the resolved proxy/task, emit documentDestroy exactly once with the intended successful-load semantics, and add controlled tests for success, rejection, stale late resolution, URL change, retry, StrictMode, and unmount that assert exact destroy-call and metric counts.

blocking_findings.finding: Render failure and unmount cleanup are incomplete. Canvas backing dimensions are allocated before getContext/page.render; a missing context or synchronous render throw returns with a nonzero, untracked canvas and no cleanup. Unmount launches asynchronous cancellation/cleanup with void and provides no completion barrier before document teardown. Existing tests do not exercise context absence, synchronous render throw, or exact cleanup order for those paths.
blocking_findings.required_fix: Roll back/zero allocated canvases and clean the page on pre-start failures, ensure every started task has one terminal outcome, and provide an awaited disposal path that completes cancel → settle → page.cleanup → canvas zero before document teardown. Add strict tests for missing context, synchronous render throw, failed promise, cancellation, eviction, and unmount.
